title: Fraction Division Word Problems
short: Decide whether a story shares a fraction or measures with one.

blocks.html: You can divide a unit fraction by a whole number and a whole number by a unit fraction. In a story, the hard part is deciding which one it is.

Ask what the story does. If a fraction is shared into equal parts, divide the fraction by the number of parts: $\frac{1}{2} \div 4$. If you measure how many pieces of a fraction size fit in an amount, divide the amount by the fraction: $4 \div \frac{1}{2}$.

Both are division, but they answer different questions. Sharing $\frac{1}{2}$ of a pizza among 4 friends gives each a small piece, $\frac{1}{8}$. Measuring how many $\frac{1}{2}$-cup scoops are in 4 cups gives a count, 8. Swapping the numbers swaps the question, so the order matters.

blocks.name: fractionbar
blocks.cap: Sharing: $\frac{1}{2}$ split into 4 equal parts. Each part is $\frac{1}{8}$.

blocks.name: numberline
blocks.cap: Measuring: how many $\frac{1}{2}$s fit in 4? Eight.

blocks.title: Sharing
blocks.q: Ana has $\frac{1}{3}$ gallon of paint. She pours it equally into 2 cans. How much is in each can?
steps: A fraction is shared into 2 parts: $\frac{1}{3} \div 2$.

blocks.title: Measuring
blocks.q: Ben has 3 yards of fabric. Each bandana takes $\frac{1}{4}$ yard. How many bandanas can he make?

blocks.html: Writing the division in the wrong order, like $4 \div \frac{1}{2}$ for “$\frac{1}{2}$ of a pizza shared by 4.” Check with sense: each friend should get less than $\frac{1}{2}$ of the pizza, not 8 pizzas.
